ruleName: Actions That Improve Conditions Affecting the Stroke
imagePrompt: Create a polished, modern semi-realistic golf illustration (about 75% realistic and 25% stylised) in the established junior golf quiz style. Show an early morning golf scene with visible dew and frost on the fairway grass. A golfer is shown about to play a shot, but is using a towel to wipe away a visible patch of dew and frost directly on the line between their ball (lying on the fairway) and the hole. The focus is on the action of wiping away the frost and dew along the intended path. Do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer on a frosty fairway uses a towel to wipe away a patch of dew and frost from the grass between their ball and the hole on a cold morning.

sceneSpec.setting: Cool early morning on a golf course fairway, with visible frost and dew on the grass.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer preparing to play a shot, holding a towel.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Golf ball at rest on the frosty grass in the fairway.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The golfer is actively wiping away a patch of dew and frost from the grass on the line between their ball and the hole.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Clarifies that players must not remove dew or frost to improve playing conditions on their line of play under Rule 8.1a.
mustShow: Visible layer of frost and dew on the fairway grass
Player using a towel to wipe away dew and frost directly on the line between ball and hole

questions.title: Can You Wipe Away Dew or Frost Before You Hit?
questions.question: It’s a chilly morning and your ball is on the fairway. There is shiny dew and frost on the grass between your ball and the hole. You use your towel to wipe off the dew and frost before you hit. What should happen?

choices.text: This is fine because dew and frost are just water.
This is fine because you are only cleaning the grass.
You get a penalty because you made it easier for yourself by wiping away the dew or frost.
You get one extra shot added to your score.

questions.explanation: You must not try to make your shot easier by wiping away dew or frost from where you will hit the ball. The rules do not let you brush away dew or frost to help you play. It’s okay if you move it by accident when you walk or swing, but not on purpose.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Tiny drops of water you see on the grass in the morning.
Ice that covers the grass when it’s very cold.
The short grass between the tee and the green.
Extra shots you get for breaking a rule.

questions.teachingTip: Show children grass with dew or frost, and practice playing shots without touching or brushing it away.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think dew and frost are loose things you can move, like leaves.
They might believe cleaning the grass is always allowed before a shot.

questions.title: Is it Allowed to Remove Dew or Frost from Your Line of Play?
questions.question: Early on a cold morning, your ball is on the fairway. There is a layer of frost and dew on the grass between your ball and the hole. Before playing, you wipe the frost away with your towel to make the shot easier. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: This is allowed because dew and frost are temporary water.
This is allowed because you are only cleaning the grass.
You receive the general penalty because you improved the conditions affecting your stroke.

questions.explanation: Dew, frost and water are not loose impediments, so you cannot deliberately remove them to improve the conditions affecting your stroke. Brushing away dew or frost from your line of play or the area where your club will swing is a breach of Rule 8. However, there is no penalty if you accidentally remove dew or frost while taking a normal stance or making your stroke.
